WHOLE_SCREEN_COHESION.note: The detailed clay town is confined to one rounded card while the pale blue-to-cream page and two white utility cards remain visually disconnected, so the screen still reads as assets placed on a menu.

ART_UI_INTEGRATION.note: The town artwork stops cleanly at a generic rounded rectangle, and its orange play button, white text, beige cards, and emoji-like symbols do not share a convincing material or shape language.

TYPOGRAPHY_QUALITY.note: The centered title has some character, but the subtitle, card labels, and badge use weakly differentiated sans-serif styles that resemble ordinary web UI.

VISUAL_HIERARCHY.note: The large illustrated card and orange circular play button establish the primary action quickly, although the card's title competes with the visually prominent white tiles immediately below.

SPACING_RHYTHM.note: The header-to-hero and hero-to-tiles gaps are controlled, but the composition occupies only the upper portion of the tall screen and leaves a large inert cream area below.

DEPTH.note: The town itself has rich modeled depth, but outside it the page consists mainly of flat color fields and lightly shadowed cards sitting on one plane.

ICON_CONSISTENCY.note: A photographic book emoji, a sprout emoji, and a custom orange play control visibly come from three different icon systems.

MOBILE_COMPOSITION.note: The hero fills the available width effectively, but the two-column utility row forces narrow cards and undersized secondary text while the lower half of the viewport remains unused.

GAME_PREMIUM_FEEL.note: The polished town illustration suggests a professional game, but the plain page shell, emoji icons, and generic utility cards make the surrounding experience resemble an educational web prototype.

AMATEURISHNESS.note: The emoji icons, muted disabled-card treatment, basic drop shadows, and abrupt separation between premium artwork and generic cards make the build feel unfinished.

WHOLE_SCREEN_COHESION.note: The entire experience is a narrow pale-blue column floating inside a much larger cream canvas, making the illustrated card and menu tiles feel assembled rather than world-like.

ART_UI_INTEGRATION.note: The illustration remains a self-contained banner with overlaid text, while the controls below revert immediately to conventional white cards with unrelated symbols.

TYPOGRAPHY_QUALITY.note: The title is clean but not strongly branded, and the smaller Japanese copy appears thin and generic against both the header and card surfaces.

VISUAL_HIERARCHY.note: The wide town card and orange play circle clearly dominate, but the primary content is physically small relative to the 1280-by-900 canvas.

SPACING_RHYTHM.note: The content cluster ends around the upper-middle of the screen, leaving hundreds of pixels of empty cream space below and broad unused margins on both sides.

DEPTH.note: The dimensional town is visually trapped inside the hero card, while the outer background, central strip, and lower cards form only shallow stacked rectangles.

ICON_CONSISTENCY.note: The book emoji, sprout emoji, and custom play triangle have incompatible rendering, scale, and visual weight.

MOBILE_COMPOSITION.note: Although this is the desktop capture, its fixed narrow content rail closely resembles a mobile layout placed at the center rather than a desktop-specific composition.

GAME_PREMIUM_FEEL.note: The high-quality town asset is undermined by the empty desktop canvas, fixed-width column, emoji navigation, and understated browser-like typography.

AMATEURISHNESS.note: The conspicuous unused desktop space, isolated central strip, mixed icon sources, and generic cards make the screen look like an early responsive web implementation.

top_3_concrete_fixes: Extend the town's visual environment beyond the hero-card boundary using a full-screen softly blurred or enlarged derivative of the existing illustration, with a readable gradient overlay, so the page background and hero feel like one continuous world.

Replace the book and sprout emoji with one consistent CSS/SVG icon set, then match both utility cards and the play control through shared stroke weight, color treatment, corner radii, and pressed/hover states.

Create responsive desktop layout rules instead of retaining the narrow mobile rail: enlarge the hero and content cluster, constrain it within a broader game-stage container, reduce the empty lower canvas, and preserve the tighter mobile spacing separately.
requires_human_product_decision: Select or commission a distinctive display typeface and supporting Japanese UI type system to establish a recognizable JIBUN CHOICE identity.
root_cause: The premium town illustration is still isolated inside a generic card-and-emoji menu shell, with the disconnection becoming especially obvious in the sparse desktop composition.
